Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old female with a several-day history of a dry, itchy rash on the arms and hands, likely dermatitis, after swimming and ongoing work-related stress; managed with emollients, topical steroids, and OTC antihistamines; no systemic symptoms; plan to re-evaluate in 1 week.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy red rash on arms and hands; started a few days ago; not improved with coconut butter; no fever or systemic symptoms; no spread to chest/legs/face; no cracking skin reported.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began several days prior; gradual onset; no improvement with prior home remedy.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Trigger possibly swimming a few days before onset; stress at work; coconut butter did not help.
- Associated symptoms: No pain, no fever, no vomiting, no bowel/urinary symptoms; appetite and energy otherwise normal aside from recent tiredness.
- ROS: Denies fever, vomiting, loose stools; reports tiredness.
- Past Medical History: No prior skin problems (eczema, dermatitis) mentioned. Currently taking Microgynon (contraceptive pill); no other medications.
- Allergies: Lactose intolerance noted.
- Medications: Microgynon (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social History: Lives alone; works as a primary school teacher; recently stressed with long work hours; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; no recreational drugs.
- Family History: Father with asthma; mother with hayfever; no known skin problems in family.
- Other notes: Possible weather changes considered by patient.

Past Medical History:
- No documented chronic skin disease (e.g., eczema, dermatitis) previously.
- Lactose intolerance reported.
- Family history of asthma and hayfever.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Dermatitis (likely irritant/contact dermatitis of the hands and arms)
  - Education: Provide patient information leaflet about dermatitis.
  - Treatments:
    - Emollients: Apply to affected skin throughout the day for the next several days.
    - Topical corticosteroid cream: Start to reduce inflammation (specific agent not named).
    - Antihistamines: OTC options (Piriton or Loratadine) to help itch.
  - Avoidance/Triggers: Consider possible trigger from swimming; note stress as contributing factor.
  - Analgesia: Paracetamol not indicated for this condition.
  - Follow-up: If symptoms do not improve, return for re-evaluation in one week.
